newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mexico sees '96 GDP growing almost four percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees '96 GDP growing almost four percent.

text.p: Mexican Commerce Secretary Herminio Blanco said on Friday his country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth should almost reach four percent in 1996 and be at least four percent in 1997.
Blanco was speaking at a lunch organised by the APEC Business Forum ahead of the annual Asia-Pacific summit in the Philippines.

Blanco said Mexico had taken painful measures to bring its economy back from its recent troubles, and was now seeing the fruits of those labours. "Mexico is clearly back on track," he told his business audience.
He said the country's economic performance was steadily improving. "In 1997...we expect a growth rate of at least four percent," he said.
"Our goal is to generate an annual growth rate of about five percent at least," he said.
He said the country's inflation rate was falling rapidly and should reach about 26 percent year on year in 1996, which he said would be half the rate for the previous year.
He said the inflation rate in 1997 was expected to be about 15 percent.
